author: Myeongjin Kang

declarations.contract: Actual finite sum of scalar multiples of additive characters.
Finite-sum sesquilinearity in the first argument of the explicitly weighted inner product.
Finite-sum linearity in the second argument of the explicitly weighted inner product.
For any finite additive commutative group G and finite index type I, injective χ:I→AddChar G ℂ gives normalized sample inner product Σ star(c_i)d_i.
The real averaged squared sample norm equals Σ||c_i||² for the same injective character family; normalization is 1/card(G).
Multiplication of both coefficient lists by u_i preserves sampled inner product if every star(u_i)u_i=1.
For u,x in finite additive G, sampling at x+u equals sampling coefficients χ_i(u)c_i at x.
Concrete additive character x↦stdAddChar(k*x) on ZMod q, q≠0.
Distinct residues k in ZMod q define distinct modes.
Actual ZMod modes selected by an injective k:I→ZMod q satisfy finite Parseval.
Fin K→ZMod q, i↦i, is injective when K≤q.
Fin(2K+1)→ZMod q, i↦i−K, is injective when 2K+1≤q; this is the one-dimensional signed band.
Actual representation g↦χ(g)⁻¹ρ(g), for a group representation ρ and unit-valued multiplicative character χ.
Actual invariant average of the twisted representation, over a finite group.
P(v)=card(G)⁻¹ Σ_g χ(g)⁻¹ρ(g)v.
Twisted invariance is equivalent to ρ(g)v=χ(g)v for every group element.
Every output P(v) has the χ-eigen transformation law.
Every vector with the χ-eigen transformation law is fixed by P.
The range of P is exactly all χ-eigen vectors.
A supplied linear R commuting with every ρ(g) commutes with P.
Actual Equiv.Perm.sign character, mapped from integer units to complex units.
For every supplied representation of permutations, its sign projector output transforms by the integer sign.
Complex sign inverse equals sign.
Explicit permutation sum with sign coefficients and division by card(Perm A).
Exact scalar p(e,t,Q)=1/2−(e−t)/(4Q).
For η≥0 the four budgets η,η/4,η/8,η/16 sum to at most2η.
Four explicitly assumed adjacent absolute scalar energy errors imply |Egrid−E|≤2η.
A scalar error at mostγ/10 reduces a +γ margin to +9γ/10.
A scalar error at mostγ/10 reduces a −γ margin to −9γ/10.
0≤w≤1,0≤p≤bound imply wp≤bound; the lower bound on w is retained for the physical interpretation but not needed algebraically.
0≤w≤1,p≥0,p≤1/2−γ and |p′−wp|≤γ/10 imply p′≤1/2−9γ/10, with failure weight retained.
The fair average of the two scalar kinetic/potential tests equals p(kinetic+potential,t,Q).
Q>0 and t−2Q≤e≤t+2Q imply 0≤p(e,t,Q)≤1.

not_formalized: Continuous torus Fourier series/integrals, physical h^(D/2) normalization, real translations and their unit-modulus phase production.
Explicit tensor-product D-dimensional grid characters and finite spin sums; the generic finite-group theorem is not an instantiated physical product grid.
Coulomb forms, Hardy estimates, nonbinding IMS/escaping-particle wedge, cap comparison, spectral-domain eigenvector/cutoff and all analytic error premises.
L2 translation bound, squared-density inequality, Lipschitz quadrature and averaging shifted grid cells, all-state operator comparison.
Concrete particle-block spatial-spin representation and its unitarity, Hilbert self-adjointness/orthogonality of sign average, odd/reflection/cutoff subspaces or their actual commutation.
Density operators, trace/accepted-weight realization, quantum instruments, permutation encoding or its polynomial circuit, QFT/approximation/circuit complexity.
Polynomial input bounds, source hardness, QMA definition/membership/completeness and entangled-witness amplification.
conditional_interfaces: Frequency injectivity is proved for concrete one-dimensional initial and centered ZMod bands, and explicitly assumed for the general character family.
Phase factors must satisfy star(u_i)u_i=1; arbitrary real-torus shifts are not constructed.
A supplied group representation and multiplicative unit-valued character are structural hypotheses; the representation laws are not assumed projector conclusions.
Commutation requires the supplied restriction R to commute with every representation operator; R need not be idempotent in that supporting theorem.
Scalar analytic bounds, positive scale, gap and acceptance-error hypotheses are explicit; no analytic fact or circuit existence is encoded as an axiom.
